summary: Audit each training-free comparison baseline (FrugalGPT, CP-Router/conformal, AutoMix, Jitkrittum L2D, ABC, DOCTOR/MSP/Chow) against its canonical paper; flag faithfulness discrepancies + concrete fixes

audits.method: CP-Router / conformal-prediction cascade routing (split-conformal selective gate; "conformal" arm of the training-free baseline bake-off)
audits.paper_ref: CP-Router: An Uncertainty-Aware Router Between LLM and LRM, arXiv:2505.19970 (canonical conformal background: Romano, Sesia, Candès, "Classification with Valid and Adaptive Coverage" / APS, NeurIPS 2020, arXiv:2006.02544)
audits.paper_rule: CP-Router (2505.19970), verified against the arXiv HTML Method section: (1) Nonconformity score is LAC, S(x,y)=1-f(y) where f(y) is the softmax prob of option y (Sec 2.1) -- NOT cumulative APS. (2) Calibration quantile q_hat = the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))/n quantile of calibration scores (Sec 2.3). (3) Prediction set C(x)={y in Y : S(x,y) <= q_hat} = {y : f(y) >= 1 - q_hat} (Eq.1). (4) Routing rule (Sec 3.1 / pseudocode line 26): route to the cheap LLM if |C(x)| <= tau (tau defaults to 1, i.e. a singleton => low uncertainty); otherwise |C(x)| > tau routes to the LRM. (5) CRITICAL: alpha is NOT fixed -- the paper's central novel contribution is Full and Binary Entropy (FBE), which selects alpha* = argmax_alpha FBE per dataset/distribution to MAXIMIZE set-size separability between easy and hard prompts (Sec 3.2, Eq.5). (6) Benchmarks are MCQA with 4 options (A-D); the GSM8K extension uses 5 (4 + "Others"). The paper makes NO statement that small-option set-size routing reduces to MSP/Chow (an earlier PDF fetch produced such a 'quote' but it was a fetch hallucination; the HTML method section contains no such sentence).
audits.our_rule: Three non-equivalent implementations exist. (A) src/analysis/ablations/gate_alt_conformal.py:42-102 -- FAITHFUL core: LAC score s=1-softmax(gold) on PMC-train (line 55), finite-sample qhat via rank ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)) (lines 58-60), builds set {opt : p>=1-q_hat} (line 93), escalates iff len(set)!=1 (line 94). Sweeps fixed alphas {0.05..0.30}; FBE only named as a future 'next step' (docstring lines 16-17, 108-109), not implemented. (B) src/analysis/ablations/gate_alt_conformal_6datasets.py:51-82 -- COLLAPSED: score()=1-top1prob (line 51-52), calibrates q_cp at err-rate alpha=1-acc (line 61, ->0.540), then routes by 'ec = sc > q_cp' (line 82) i.e. escalate iff top1prob < 1-q_cp. This builds NO prediction set; it is a pure MSP/Chow threshold. (C) src/cascade_methods/gate_compare.py:85 -- 'conformal' arm returns 1-top1prob with comment 'LAC nonconformity (approx MSP)'; src/cascade_methods/methods.py:88-97 Conformal class uses score=1-top1prob; both are pure MSP, no set built. (D) The published 'monotone => equals MSP' assertion: src/cascade_methods/sota_comparison.py:156-157 prints 'for ...-option MCQ the set-size decision is monotone in top1prob => its frontier == MSP/Chow above; reported as that row.' The most faithful version (set_size with TAU_SET=1 + an actual fbe() + alpha* selection) lives only in src/analysis/ablations/gate_ablation_bakeoff.py:25,66-75,211-215, which needs 32B-on-calibration labels.
discrepancies: The 'equals MSP' claim is only conditionally true and is presented as unconditional. LAC set-size with tau=1 equals an MSP threshold ONLY when the inclusion threshold 1-q_hat >= 0.5 (then at most one option can be included, so |C|=1 iff top1prob>=1-q_hat). I verified this on the actual checkpoints: at the err-rate alpha=0.54 used by gate_alt_conformal_6datasets.py the threshold is 0.744 (>0.5) so set-size and MSP agree on 100% of 8220 eval samples -- but at the tighter alphas CP-Router targets the rules DIVERGE: alpha=0.20 ->2.0% disagreement, 0.15 ->5.8%, 0.10 ->9.7%, 0.05 ->17.6% of eval decisions differ. So 'monotone in top1prob' is false in exactly the regime CP-Router operates in.

The stated precondition '<=5-option MCQ' is factually wrong for our data. The eval opt_logprobs dicts contain 5-10 options (distribution: 8 opts x5307, 9 x1402, 10 x897, 7 x536, 6 x76, 5 x2). The 4-option premise only holds for the PMC-train calibration set, not the 8220-sample eval the gate scores. With 8+ options and a sub-0.5 inclusion threshold, |C|>=2 is common, breaking MSP-equivalence (consistent with the 17.6% divergence).

CP-Router's defining contribution -- per-dataset FBE selection of alpha* to maximize set-size separability -- is NOT implemented in any arm that feeds a reported comparison row. gate_alt_conformal.py fixes/sweeps alpha; gate_alt_conformal_6datasets.py and the gate_compare/methods 'conformal' arms fix alpha at the err-rate and don't even build a set. An fbe() exists only in gate_ablation_bakeoff.py (Part B, needs 32B-on-calib). The reported 'conformal' baseline is therefore CP-Router-without-CP-Router's-novelty.

Whether the reported 'conformal' row is the faithful set-size implementation (gate_alt_conformal.py) or the MSP-collapsed one (gate_alt_conformal_6datasets.py / gate_compare.py) is ambiguous across files; sota_comparison.py explicitly folds CP-Router INTO the MSP/Chow row rather than running set-size at a tuned alpha.

Nonconformity-score choice (LAC vs APS) matches the CP-Router paper (LAC, S=1-f(y)) and is fine; but note Romano-2020 APS would give different, generally larger sets and is the more standard adaptive choice -- not a fidelity bug, just worth stating which score is claimed.
audits.fix: Report the FAITHFUL set-size implementation as the CP-Router row, not the MSP collapse. Concretely: (1) In sota_comparison.py delete the lines 156-157 'monotone => == MSP/Chow' note and instead run gate_alt_conformal.py's set-size rule (build C(x)={p>=1-q_hat}, escalate iff |C|!=1) as its own row. (2) Implement CP-Router's actual alpha selection: add the fbe() from gate_ablation_bakeoff.py:70-75 and choose alpha* = argmax_alpha FBE(set_sizes on the LABEL-FREE eval/calib pool) per dataset, rather than fixing alpha at the 7B err-rate -- this is the paper's whole point and currently exists only in the orphaned Part-B bakeoff. (3) In gate_alt_conformal_6datasets.py:82 and gate_compare.py:85 / methods.py:92-97, either build a real prediction set or relabel these arms honestly as 'MSP/Chow' (they are not conformal). (4) If you keep an 'equals MSP' caveat anywhere, gate it correctly: 'equal to MSP ONLY when 1-q_hat>=0.5; at the alphas FBE selects the set-size rule differs from MSP on up to ~18% of decisions and the eval has 5-10 options, not <=5.' Acceptable interim alternative: present the conformal row from gate_alt_conformal.py (faithful score+set+quantile) and footnote that FBE adaptivity is not yet added, rather than claiming equivalence to MSP.

audits.method: FrugalGPT cascade with learned reliability scorer (the "learned-correct" / learned-GBM arm)
audits.paper_ref: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance (Chen, Zaharia, Zou 2023), arXiv:2305.05176
audits.paper_rule: FrugalGPT's "LLM cascade" arranges LLM APIs cheapest-first. A learned scoring function g(q,a): Q x A -> [0,1] (a DistilBERT tuned for regression, much cheaper than the LLMs) takes the query AND the LLM's GENERATED ANSWER TEXT and outputs a reliability/correctness score. Cascade rule: "It returns the generation if the score is higher than a threshold tau_i, and queries the next service otherwise" (HEADLINES example: accept GPT-J if score>0.96, else J1-L if >0.37, else GPT-4). The scorer is "a simple regression model that learns whether a generation is correct from the query and a generated answer" (binary correctness labels). Cascade composition L and threshold vector tau are chosen by a constrained optimization: max E[r(a, f_Lz(q))] s.t. E[cost] <= b (budget b is a user parameter, not tuned on test). Protocol: "Each dataset is randomly split into a training set to learn the LLM cascade and a test set for evaluation." So: scorer trained on train split, thresholds optimized on train split under a budget constraint, evaluated on a disjoint held-out test split.
audits.our_rule: Two implementations. (A) src/analysis/ablations/gate_alt_learned_gbm.py (+ _6datasets.py): HistGradientBoostingClassifier on a 12-dim feature vector from 7B opt_logprobs only (margin, entropy, sorted 10-dim option-logprob distribution) -> clf.fit(Xtr, ytr) where Xtr/ytr come from ckpts/gate_7b_pmctrain (3000 PMC-VQA-TRAIN rows, ok labels); tau set by error-rate budget on TRAIN: tau = np.quantile(clf.predict_proba(Xtr)[:,1], err) with err=1-ytr.mean(); then frozen and applied unchanged to held-out eval sets (escalate when P_hat(correct) < tau). (B) src/cascade_methods/gate_compare.py, method "learned-correct": per tier, make_pipeline(StandardScaler, LogisticRegression).fit(feat(s)[cal], P["ok"][cal]) on an 8-dim logprob-shape feature set (FEATS = margin, maxlogprob, top1prob, prob_margin, entropy, entropy2, gini, n_opts); escalation score = -P_hat(this tier correct); thresholds (t0,t1) grid-searched on the cal half only to reach calib-parity at min latency, then applied to the disjoint te=~cal half; honest 50/50 calib/test split, 20 seeds; parity target tgt=P["ok2"][cal].mean() also computed on calib.
discrepancies: INPUT MODALITY (the core deviation, present in BOTH files): FrugalGPT's scorer g(q,a) is a DistilBERT that reads the QUERY plus the GENERATED ANSWER TEXT to judge reliability/correctness. Our scorer reads ONLY the model's per-letter logprob shape (margin/entropy/distribution in the GBM file; 8 logprob-shape features in gate_compare). We never feed query or answer text to a learned model. This makes our 'learned' arm a logprob-confidence classifier, not a text-reliability scorer. It is a defensible stand-in for multiple-choice VQA (correctness is largely determined by which letter wins, captured by logprobs) and is arguably a STRONGER-than-paper variant for MCQA, but it is not the same mechanism and should be labeled as an adaptation, not 'FrugalGPT'.

DECISION RULE SIGN/DIRECTION is faithful: paper accepts when score>tau (escalate when score<=tau); both our files escalate when P_hat(correct) is low (gate_compare uses score=-P_hat so 'score>t0' == 'P_hat<threshold'; GBM uses 'Pl < tau'). Equivalent.

THRESHOLD SELECTION protocol: paper learns thresholds on TRAIN under a budget constraint, evaluates on disjoint TEST. (A) GBM file: tau is set on PMC-TRAIN by an error-rate quantile and frozen -> faithful to 'learn on train, apply on test', actually a transfer-stress version (calibrated on PMC-train, applied cross-dataset). (B) gate_compare: thresholds chosen on the cal half to hit calib-parity, applied to the held-out te half -> faithful 50/50 split. NO threshold-selection-on-test in either file.

LEAKAGE CHECK: clean in both. (A) GBM: trained and tau-set entirely on PMC-VQA-TRAIN (ckpts/gate_7b_pmctrain, 3000 rows), which CLAUDE.md confirms is held out from all eval samples; applied unchanged to eval. (B) gate_compare: scorer .fit on feat[cal] with ok[cal], thresholds searched on cal, evaluated on te=~cal; parity target also from cal. No eval labels touch training or threshold selection.

OBJECTIVE FRAMING differs but is benign: paper maximizes reward s.t. a cost BUDGET b; we instead fix iso-accuracy (calib-parity to always-32B-think) and minimize latency/FLOPs. This is the dual/swapped form of the same accuracy-cost tradeoff and matches the project's stated metric (escalation/cost at iso-accuracy with per-benchmark guardrail). Not a faithfulness problem, but worth stating that the operating point is chosen differently from the paper's budget knob.

GBM tau uses a single global error-rate quantile on PMC-train rather than a per-dataset budget; this is a reasonable single-operating-point choice and not leakage, but the cross-dataset application means the realized escalation rate on other benchmarks is not budget-controlled (this is exactly the 'transfer collapse' the script is designed to expose).
audits.fix: Faithfulness is acceptable for an MCQA ablation; the one substantive thing to fix is LABELING/FRAMING, not code. (1) In the paper-comparison text and any results table, do not call this 'FrugalGPT' verbatim; call it 'FrugalGPT-style learned scorer (logprob-feature variant)' and add one sentence: FrugalGPT's DistilBERT reads query+generated-answer TEXT; for multiple-choice VQA we substitute a learned classifier on the answer-distribution logprobs, which captures MCQA correctness and avoids running a separate text model. This is the honest delta. (2) Optional strengthening if a reviewer pushes: add a true text-reliability variant by fitting a small classifier on the raw generated answer string / option text (we store raw_output in the JSONL) to show the logprob variant is not weaker. (3) Keep both threshold protocols as-is — gate_compare's calib/test split and the GBM's train-frozen tau are both leakage-free and the GBM's cross-dataset frozen-tau is the more honest (harder) transfer test, so prefer reporting gate_compare for the iso-accuracy comparison and the GBM file for the transfer-collapse ablation. (4) Consider noting that we optimize at iso-accuracy/min-cost rather than max-reward/budget-b (dual of the paper's objective) so the comparison axis is explicit.

audits.method: Learning-to-defer / post-hoc deferral (predict benefit P(strong correct) − P(weak correct) and defer when it exceeds a cost threshold). Implemented as the "learned-defer (VADR)" arm in gate_compare.py and the "meta-Δ" router in metarouter_honest.py.
audits.paper_ref: Primary: Jitkrittum, Gupta, Menon, Narasimhan, Rawat, Kumar, "When Does Confidence-Based Cascade Deferral Suffice?", NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2307.02764. Foundations: Mozannar & Sontag, "Consistent Estimators for Learning to Defer to an Expert", ICML 2020 (arXiv:2006.01862). Bi-directional proxy: Warren & Dras, "Bi-directional Model Cascading with Proxy Confidence", arXiv:2504.19391.
audits.paper_rule: Bayes-optimal deferral (Jitkrittum Prop. 3.1): r*(x) = 1[ η^(2)_{h(x)}(x) − η^(1)_{h(x)}(x) > c ], i.e. defer iff P(model-2 correct on x) − P(model-1 correct on x) exceeds a cost threshold c≥0. Since η^(2) is unavailable, they fit a post-hoc scorer g(x) and defer when g(x) > c. Table 1 estimators: "Diff-01" regresses target z = 1[y=h^(2)(x)] − 1[y=h^(1)(x)] under MSE; "Diff-Prob" regresses z = p^(2)_y(x) − p^(1)_y(x) under MAE; deferral rule in all cases is g(x) > c. Crucially: "we train g on a held-out validation set" S_val = {(x_i, z_i)} that is SEPARATE from the test set on which deferral is evaluated; the threshold c is the only quantity swept to trace the cost/deferral curve, and c is a fixed operating point (set on validation), not re-optimized per test point. Mozannar–Sontag: the same defer-when-expert-is-better target, learned via a Bayes-consistent surrogate, on a train split disjoint from evaluation. Bi-directional proxy (2504.19391): combine the small model's post-invocation confidence with a tiny proxy estimate of the LARGE model's confidence, with proxy and confidence estimators trained on held-out data, then applied to unseen test items.
audits.our_rule: gate_compare.py:learned-defer (gate_scores, lines 92-98): per tier, fit four logistic-on-logprob-signal models on the calib mask only — p0c=P̂(ok0), p0n=P̂(ok1) for T0; p1c=P̂(ok1), p1n=P̂(ok2) for T1 — and return scores (p0n−p0c),(p1n−p1c). This is exactly the Diff-Prob/Diff-01 target P̂(next-tier right)−P̂(this-tier right). Thresholds (t0,t1) are chosen on the CALIB half to reach calib-parity at min latency (main, lines 112-130) and APPLIED to the test half (lines 131-138). Faithful protocol. metarouter_honest.py:meta-Δ (eval_split, lines 107-119): fit(feats,a32)−fit(feats,a7) where fit() trains LogisticRegression on X[calib] against target[calib] (lines 107-110) — correct held-out Δ target. BUT the operating point/threshold is selected inside measure() (lines 72-106) on the TEST half: it sorts score[test], builds acc_curve over a7t/a32t (TEST labels), finds the smallest k whose pooled TEST acc ≥ target=a32t.mean() (TEST parity), and reports that k/len as the escalation rate (lines 76-84); the guardrail-constrained kg is likewise scanned over TEST labels (lines 93-104). The SOTA margin baseline gets the same test-side threshold sweep (line 113), so the head-to-head is internally fair, but the absolute reported escalation@parity is an oracle/post-hoc operating point, not a deployable one.
discrepancies: TARGET — FAITHFUL: both arms regress P̂(strong/next-tier correct) − P̂(weak/this-tier correct), matching Jitkrittum's Diff-Prob/Diff-01 and the Bayes-optimal η^(2)−η^(1) target; gate_compare's 3-tier (p0n−p0c),(p1n−p1c) is a valid per-tier generalization.

ESTIMATOR FIT — FAITHFUL: in both files the Δ-predictors (P̂(ok)) are fit only on the calib/train mask (X[calib], target[calib]); test items never enter model fitting, so the surrogate-fit step has no leakage.

THRESHOLD SELECTION — LEAKAGE in metarouter_honest.py: the escalation threshold/operating point is chosen on the TEST half using test correctness labels (measure() sweeps score[test] to the smallest k reaching test-set parity a32t.mean(), and the guardrail kg scans test labels too). The paper sets c on a held-out validation set; here c is effectively re-optimized per test fold against test labels. This violates the paper's train/validation/test separation for the DECISION threshold, despite the file being named *_honest. gate_compare.py does NOT have this issue (threshold fixed on calib, applied to test).

32B-LABEL SOURCING — partial: the per-x 32B-correctness regression labels (a32) come from the eval pool's own 32B run, then split 50/50; the calib-half labels are legitimate held-out training signal, but in metarouter_honest the test-half a32 labels additionally drive the threshold (the leakage above). gate_compare sources ok1/ok2 labels likewise and uses only the calib half for both fitting and thresholding (clean).

SURROGATE LOSS — minor: paper uses MSE (Diff-01) / MAE (Diff-Prob) to regress the signed benefit directly; we instead fit two calibrated logistic-CE correctness probabilities and subtract them. This recovers the same η^(2)−η^(1) target and is a defensible plug-in estimator (closer in spirit to Diff-Prob than a single MSE regressor), so it is a faithful variant, not a discrepancy that biases the comparison.

SCOPE NOTE: bi-directional proxy (2504.19391) is only loosely matched — we estimate the strong leg's correctness from the CHEAP model's logprob signals (a learned proxy of the strong leg), not from a separate tiny proxy model or the strong model's hidden states; acceptable as a feature-based proxy but worth stating explicitly if cited.
audits.fix: Fix metarouter_honest.py so the operating point is chosen WITHOUT test labels, mirroring gate_compare.py and the paper's held-out-validation protocol: (1) In eval_split, choose the threshold on the CALIB half — use the existing thr_min_esc_at_parity(score[calib], a7[calib], a32[calib]) (already defined, lines 48-58, but currently unused) to get tau, then APPLY it to test: esc = score[test] > tau; report esc.mean(), acc=np.where(esc,a32t,a7t).mean(), and the guardrail check on the resulting fixed-threshold escalation — never search test labels for k. (2) Apply the identical calib-chosen-threshold protocol to the SOTA margin baseline so the comparison stays fair. (3) For the guardrail-constrained variant, pick kg/threshold on calib (pooled calib parity AND per-benchmark calib acc ≥ calib 7B acc) and apply to test. After this change the reported test esc%@parity becomes a deployable operating point and the file's "honest" claim holds. gate_compare.py needs no change — it is already faithful; optionally note that its 3-tier benefit uses single-step next-tier targets (P(ok1) for T0, P(ok2) for T1) rather than full downstream-reachable correctness, which is a reasonable greedy approximation but could be documented.

audits.method: AutoMix (few-shot self-verification P(True) + meta-verifier / POMDP routing)
audits.paper_ref: AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models, Madaan, Aggarwal et al., arXiv:2310.12963 (NeurIPS 2024)
audits.paper_rule: AutoMix has TWO defining contributions. (1) FEW-SHOT SELF-VERIFICATION: the SAME small model re-reads its own answer with a 3-shot in-context prompt ("Your task is to evaluate if the AI Generated Answer is correct, based on the provided context and question. Choose between Correct or Incorrect."), producing a noisy verifier probability v = p(correct=1 | answer, context, question); for black-box models v is estimated by sampling k>1 generations at temperature. (2) META-VERIFIER over the noisy v (the paper's headline second contribution, motivated by "self-verification can be noisy"): Threshold variant m_t(v)=1 (trust SLM, no escalation) if v>=t else 0 (escalate); and the principled POMDP variant with three hidden states {Simple, Complex, Unsolvable}, observation = v, a belief distribution and a learned policy (from as few as ~50 examples) with per-state rewards (the "Unsolvable-aware" deferral logic that avoids escalating questions the large model also cannot solve). ROUTING: run SLM -> compute v -> if meta-verify(v) returns TRUE keep SLM answer, else escalate to the large LM. Escalation is driven by LOW VERIFIED CONFIDENCE, with the meta-verifier as the decision layer between v and the route.
audits.our_rule: No faithful AutoMix method exists in the repo. The self-verification SIGNAL is produced by src/labeling/run_7b_selfverify_vllm.py: a ZERO-SHOT, single-forward-pass grader prompt (SYS_VERIFY = "You are a careful medical exam grader... Respond with only 'Yes' or 'No'.", body ends "Is the proposed answer correct? Answer Yes or No.", verify_prompt() lines 79-90), reading one-token logprobs and storing p_yes_norm = p_yes/(p_yes+p_no) (yn()/main loop lines ~163-184). There are NO in-context/few-shot examples and NO k-sample temperature averaging (SamplingParams temperature=0.0, max_tokens=2). The signal is then consumed ONLY as one feature among ~10 inside the project's OWN learned deferral router: metarouter_honest.py:eval_split feeds 'verify' into a StandardScaler+LogisticRegression that predicts P(7B-correct) and P(32B-correct) and escalates on Delta=P32-P7 (lines 110-119, fit()); metarouter.py and frontier_compare.py do the same. grep confirms NO file thresholds the verified confidence alone, and there is NO meta-verifier, NO POMDP, and NO kNN anywhere (grep for pomdp/knn/meta-verif returns nothing in code). The repo's own docs label this 'VADR / AutoMix-style' but explicitly treat verify as a learned-router feature, not as AutoMix.
discrepancies: Self-verification prompt is ZERO-SHOT (single Yes/No grader system prompt), but AutoMix's first contribution is explicitly a FEW-SHOT (3-shot in-context) self-verification. The few-shot framing is the paper's title-level claim ('few-shot self-verification mechanism').

P(True) is a single greedy forward pass at temperature=0 reading one Yes/No logprob; AutoMix estimates v for black-box models by sampling k>1 generations at higher temperature. (Minor for a white-box logprob model, but it is not the paper's prescribed estimator.)

The META-VERIFIER is entirely absent. This is AutoMix's SECOND and headline contribution ('given that self-verification can be noisy, it employs a POMDP-based router'). Neither the POMDP nor even the simple threshold-on-v meta-verifier is implemented.

The routing rule does not match. AutoMix routes small->large on LOW VERIFIED CONFIDENCE (v below threshold / meta-verifier says not-TRUE). Our pipeline never routes on v at all: v is fed as one input feature to a supervised logistic Delta-predictor (P32-P7) trained on 7B/32B correctness labels. That is a learned deferral router (closer to Jitkrittum/FrugalGPT learned scorer), not AutoMix self-verification routing.

Consequence for the comparison: there is no row in the bake-off that represents AutoMix as published. The closest analog ('meta-Delta +verify') BURIES the AutoMix signal inside a different, stronger learned method, so any 'AutoMix lost / verify is weak' conclusion does not actually evaluate AutoMix's own decision rule (self-verify -> meta-verifier -> route). The repo docs (METHOD_deferral_router.md, FINDINGS.md) do correctly note verify is weak at predicting 7B-correctness (AUC 0.65-0.70), but that is a property of our zero-shot single-pass signal, not of AutoMix-with-meta-verifier.
audits.fix: Add a standalone, paper-faithful AutoMix baseline rather than only using verify as a router feature. Concretely: (1) Make the self-verification few-shot: prepend 2-3 fixed in-context (question, options, proposed answer, Correct/Incorrect) exemplars to verify_prompt() in run_7b_selfverify_vllm.py so it matches the paper's few-shot mechanism; optionally estimate v by sampling k>1 at temperature for parity with the black-box estimator (or document that the white-box single-pass p_yes_norm is the logprob equivalent). (2) Implement the meta-verifier as its own escalation method in the harness: at minimum the THRESHOLD variant -- escalate iff p_yes_norm < t, sweep t to the iso-accuracy/min-escalation operating point exactly like SOTA prob_margin (i.e. add out['AutoMix (verify-threshold)'] = measure(-P['sig']['verify']) in metarouter_honest.py / a harness method). Ideally also add the POMDP/3-state (Simple/Complex/Unsolvable) router fit on the calib half (it needs only ~50 examples) so the 'Unsolvable-aware' deferral is represented. (3) Report that standalone AutoMix row in the published comparison so 'margin gate beats AutoMix' reflects AutoMix's actual decision rule, not a learned Delta-router that merely ingests the verify feature. Until (2) exists, claims that AutoMix loses to the margin gate are not supported by a faithful AutoMix implementation.

audits.method: Agreement-Based Cascading (ABC) — used as the "ACC-v2 / agreement" think-tier gate in our cascade
audits.paper_ref: "Agreement-Based Cascading for Efficient Inference" (Kolawole, Dennis, Talwalkar, Smith), arXiv:2407.02348 (v3)
audits.paper_rule: Each cascade level is an ensemble H^k of k>=1 models from the same hypothesis class. The deferral/escalation decision is intra-level agreement: vote(x;H^k) = (1/k) * sum_{h in H^k} 1[H^k(x) = h(x)] (fraction of same-level ensemble members agreeing with the level's MAJORITY prediction). Voting rule: r_v(x;theta_v) = 1[vote(x;H^k_1) <= theta_v] (defer/escalate when agreement falls below threshold); score rule r_s analogously on the average score of the majority prediction. "When a (configurable) fraction of models in a tier agree, it signals that they likely have the right answer. Conversely, if they disagree, the uncertainty triggers a deferral to the next, more powerful ensemble." Agreement is STRICTLY among same-level ensemble members (the paper never compares a small model vs a large model across levels). On agreement the output is the ensemble's majority prediction y <- H_i(x). theta is fit on ~100 unseen validation samples.
audits.our_rule: acc_v2.py: think_score(P) = P["disagree"] + 1e-6*(-P["m1"]) where disagree = 1[pred_7B-nt != pred_32B-nt] (line 62, 82); escalate to think iff think_score > tau1 (route(), line ~86). Same rule in acc_compare.py M1b (line 133: s1 = P["disagree"] + 1e-6*(-P["m_32n"]); e1 = e0 & (s1 > t1)). tau1 calibrated on held-out 50/50 calib (20 seeds) to reach always-32B-think parity at min escalation. On agreement the cascade keeps the 32B-no-think answer (the larger of the two voters), not a symmetric majority vote. peer_router.py uses the same agreement primitive more broadly: pairwise agreement flags ag_7iv/ag_7phi/ag_ivphi as features for a learned router, plus an interpretable "agree->trust answer; disagree->7B unless margin<tau then peer" rule (lines 80-105).
discrepancies: Voter composition / locus of agreement: ABC measures agreement AMONG k same-level (similar-cost) ensemble members at a single tier; our gate measures agreement BETWEEN two models that sit at DIFFERENT tiers (cheap 7B-nt at tier 0 vs expensive 32B-nt at tier 1). The paper explicitly does NOT implement cross-level small-vs-large agreement — that cross-level 'consistency/deferral' pattern is a related-but-distinct line. So ours is an ABC-flavored cross-tier consistency check, not ABC's intra-level ensemble vote.

Ensemble size: ABC's canonical instantiation uses ensembles of k>1 distinct same-class models per level; ours is a single pairwise (k=2) comparison. Mechanically, ABC's vote() reduces exactly to 1[agree] when k=2 and both predictions are compared (vote=1.0 if agree, 0.5 if disagree, so vote<=theta for any theta in [0.5,1) is precisely 'disagree'), so the binary disagree-escalate rule IS the k=2 special case of ABC's voting rule — but it is the minimal/degenerate ensemble.

Output-on-agreement: ABC outputs the ensemble MAJORITY prediction; our cascade outputs the 32B-no-think answer specifically (the larger model already decoded at that tier). This is asymmetric, not a vote aggregate.

Added tiebreak not in ABC: the epsilon*(-m_32B-nt) term makes the gate fire only on the LOWEST-margin disagreements (think ~14% not the full ~32% disagreement rate). This blends ABC-style disagreement with the score/confidence rule rather than using pure vote<=theta.

Diversity assumption: ABC's agreement signal is meaningful via ensemble member diversity; the paper does not stress independence, but our two voters are same-FAMILY (both MedVLThinker RL_m23k, 7B vs 32B) and thus correlated, which weakens the query-by-committee interpretation — though peer_router.py separately tests genuinely cross-family voters (InternVL2.5-8B, Phi-3.5-V).
audits.fix: No code change required for faithfulness of the escalation mechanism: the binary disagree-escalate rule is the exact k=2 special case of ABC's vote(x;H^k)<=theta rule, and the credit is handled correctly (see below). The only changes worth making are framing/wording, not code: (1) In METHOD_ACC.md / METHOD_MATH.md, describe the gate as a 'k=2 cross-tier instantiation of ABC's voting rule' rather than implying it is ABC's canonical intra-level ensemble agreement, and note the answer-on-agreement is asymmetric (32B-nt), so a reviewer is not misled into thinking we reproduce ABC's ensemble-majority setup. (2) Note that the epsilon-margin tiebreak is a hybrid of ABC's vote rule and its score rule (s(x)<=theta_s), i.e. we use BOTH ABC rules, not just vote. These are accuracy-of-description fixes. The novelty disclaimer is already correct and should stay.

audits.method: Confidence baselines: Chow's rule (1970), MSP (Hendrycks & Gimpel 2017), predictive entropy, and DOCTOR (Granese et al. NeurIPS 2021) D_alpha (Gini) / D_beta detectors, implemented in signals_from_logprobs (src/cascade_methods/harness.py) and mapped to gate scores in methods.py, sota_comparison.py, gate_compare.py, final_comparison.py.
audits.paper_ref: Chow, "On Optimum Recognition Error and Reject Tradeoff," IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 1970 (no arXiv). Hendrycks & Gimpel, "A Baseline for Detecting Misclassified and Out-of-Distribution Examples in Neural Networks," ICLR 2017, arXiv:1610.02136. Granese et al., "DOCTOR: A Simple Method for Detecting Misclassification Errors," NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2106.02395.
audits.paper_rule: MSP (1610.02136): confidence = max_y softmax(x)_y; flag/reject when it is LOW. Chow (1970): optimal reject rule accepts iff the maximum a-posteriori probability max_y P(y|x) > threshold, else reject; reject score = 1 - max_y P(y|x). Entropy: predictive entropy H(p) = -sum_y p_y log p_y over the class distribution; higher = less confident. DOCTOR (2106.02395, Definition 2 / Eq. 14): with g_hat(x) defined by 1 - g_hat(x) = 1 - sum_y softmax^2(x)_y (so g_hat = sum_y softmax(x)_y^2, the squared l2-norm of the softmax over ALL classes y in Y), D_alpha(x,gamma) = 1[1 - g_hat(x) > gamma * g_hat(x)] = 1[1 - sum_y softmax^2 > gamma * sum_y softmax^2]; D_beta(x,gamma) = 1[Pe_hat(x) > gamma*(1 - Pe_hat(x))] with Pe_hat = 1 - max_y softmax(x)_y, i.e. 1[1 - max softmax > gamma*max softmax]. In the Totally Black Box (TBB) scenario only the soft-predictions are used, with no temperature scaling or input perturbation (PBB adds those). The quantity 1 - sum p^2 is exactly the Gini impurity, so D_alpha is a threshold on the Gini impurity.
audits.our_rule: harness.py signals_from_logprobs (lines 86-95): from the stored per-letter logprob dict it forms vals=sorted(logprobs,desc), then a renormalized softmax over the PRESENT option letters p = exp(vals-max)/sum, and computes top1prob=p[0], prob_margin=p[0]-p[1], entropy=-(p*log p).sum(), gini=1-(p*p).sum(), margin=vals[0]-vals[1] (raw-logprob gap), neg_energy=-logsumexp. Gate mappings: MSP/Chow = -top1prob (sota_comparison.py:69, gate_compare.py:82, methods.py:22); entropy = +entropy (sota_comparison.py:70); Gini/DOCTOR = +gini (sota_comparison.py:71, gate_compare.py:84); methods.py:21 separately labels maxlogprob as 'Chow's rule / max-logit'. Thresholds chosen by quantile/sweep (e.g. honest_point in sota_comparison.py:89-107; min_bb_at_parity:76). The opt_logprobs are vLLM top-20 token logprobs at the answer position filtered to letters A-J (src/sweep/run_7b_prune_sweep.py opt_lp:94-101); empirically they already sum to ~1.0 (min 0.953, median 0.9998 over 8220 rows). 32B labels carry empty opt_logprobs, so all gates score the 7B's distribution only.
discrepancies: MSP / Chow: correct. -top1prob escalates on low max softmax prob = exactly MSP, and equals 1-max P(y|x) up to sign = Chow's optimal-reject score. Since the gate thresholds the score, sign-flip vs additive offset is immaterial. The 'MSP/Chow' merge is fair: under quantile/sweep thresholding both reduce to the identical max-prob threshold.

DOCTOR D_alpha = Gini: FAITHFUL and even verified monotone-equivalent. Paper Eq.14 D_alpha = 1[1-sum p^2 > gamma*sum p^2]; algebra gives D_alpha fires iff gini=1-sum p^2 > gamma/(1+gamma), a strictly-increasing threshold on gini. Our 'Gini/DOCTOR = +gini' with a swept/quantile threshold therefore reproduces D_alpha's decision rule exactly for the corresponding gamma. Our setting (stored softmax, no gradients/temperature) is precisely DOCTOR's TBB scenario, which is the apples-to-apples one to use.

DOCTOR D_beta is NOT implemented as a separate row. D_beta thresholds Pe_hat=1-max softmax, which is monotone in top1prob, so it is decision-identical to MSP/Chow under thresholding and is implicitly covered by the MSP/Chow row. This is a labeling completeness gap, not a correctness bug; if D_beta were listed separately it would tie MSP/Chow exactly. Worth a one-line note in the paper so readers do not expect a distinct number.

Normalization domain: paper's g_hat is sum over the FULL class set Y; our softmax is renormalized over the PRESENT option letters only. For MCQ the answer options ARE the label set, so renormalizing over options is the correct task interpretation; and the captured letters hold >=95.3% of probability mass (median 99.98%), so renorm vs raw-prob differs by at most 0.025 in gini (mean 0.0002) over all 8220 rows. No truncation bias, no degenerate single-letter rows.

Units label nuance (cosmetic): 'margin' = top1-top2 of raw LOGPROBS, while 'prob_margin' = top1-top2 of PROBABILITIES. Both are present, both correctly computed, and the code comments/keys distinguish them. 'margin' (the deployed gate) is a logprob gap, not the FrugalGPT prob-margin; sota_comparison.py labels it 'margin(FrugalGPT)' which slightly conflates the two but they are reported as separate rows so the comparison is not biased.
entropy: standard Shannon entropy of the renormalized option distribution, +entropy escalates on high entropy. Correct, matches predictive-entropy baseline.
audits.fix: No correctness fix required - the implementations are faithful. Recommended (cosmetic) improvements for the paper: (1) Add a sentence noting DOCTOR D_beta is decision-equivalent to MSP/Chow under threshold selection (Pe_hat=1-max softmax is monotone in MSP), and that DOCTOR D_alpha equals a threshold on Gini impurity (verified: fires iff gini>gamma/(1+gamma)), so the 'Gini/DOCTOR' row IS D_alpha in the TBB scenario. (2) State explicitly in the methods/caption that softmax is renormalized over the answer options (the MCQ label set) and that the stored top-20-letter mass is >=95% (median ~100%), so the renormalization vs full-vocab softmax is a near-identity (max gini delta 0.025). (3) Optionally rename 'margin(FrugalGPT)' to 'logprob-margin' to avoid conflation with prob_margin. None of these change any reported number.

must_fix.issue: There is NO faithful AutoMix in the repo, yet it is treated as a defeated baseline. AutoMix's two defining contributions are (a) FEW-SHOT (3-shot) self-verification and (b) a META-VERIFIER (threshold-on-v, and a POMDP over {Simple,Complex,Unsolvable}). Our only verify signal is run_7b_selfverify_vllm.py: a ZERO-SHOT single greedy forward pass (temp=0, no in-context exemplars, no k-sample averaging). grep for few-shot|pomdp|meta-verif|knn returns nothing in code. The signal is then consumed ONLY as one feature among ~10 inside our own learned Delta-router (metarouter_honest.py eval_split, fit() lines 107-119), never thresholded on v alone. So no row evaluates AutoMix's actual decision rule (self-verify -> meta-verifier -> route); 'margin gate beats AutoMix' / 'verify is weak' is unsupported because the AutoMix signal is buried inside a different, stronger learned method.
must_fix.fix: Add a standalone paper-faithful AutoMix row before publishing the comparison: (1) make verify_prompt few-shot (prepend 2-3 fixed (question, options, proposed answer, Correct/Incorrect) exemplars), optionally k-sample at temperature or document that white-box p_yes_norm is the logprob equivalent; (2) implement the meta-verifier as its own escalation method — at minimum the THRESHOLD variant: out['AutoMix (verify-threshold)'] = measure(-P['sig']['verify']), swept to iso-accuracy/min-escalation exactly like SOTA prob_margin; ideally also the 3-state POMDP fit on the calib half (~50 examples) for the Unsolvable-aware deferral; (3) report that standalone row. Until this exists, do not claim margin beats AutoMix.

must_fix.issue: Threshold-selection leakage in a file named *_honest. The Delta-predictors are fit cleanly on the calib mask only (fit(), X[calib]), but the OPERATING POINT is chosen on the TEST half against TEST labels: measure() sorts score[test], builds acc_curve over a7t/a32t (test correctness), and reports the smallest k reaching test-set parity a32t.mean(); the guardrail kg is likewise scanned over test labels. The paper (Jitkrittum NeurIPS 2023) sets the cost threshold c on a held-out VALIDATION set and only evaluates on test. So the reported esc%@parity is an oracle/post-hoc operating point, not deployable. The SOTA margin baseline gets the same test-side sweep (internally fair head-to-head) but the absolute numbers are inflated for every method in this file. Confirmed: thr_min_esc_at_parity (the correct calib-side picker, line 48) is defined but used ZERO times elsewhere. NOTE: gate_compare.py's learned-defer is clean (threshold chosen on cal, applied to te).
must_fix.fix: Make the operating point calib-chosen: in eval_split, call the existing-but-unused thr_min_esc_at_parity(score[calib], a7[calib], a32[calib]) to get tau, then apply to test (esc = score[test] > tau) and report esc.mean()/acc/guardrail on that fixed threshold — never search test labels for k. Apply the identical calib-chosen-threshold to the SOTA margin baseline so the comparison stays fair. For the guardrail variant, pick kg/threshold on calib (pooled calib parity AND per-benchmark calib acc >= calib 7B acc) and apply to test. After this the 'honest' name holds. Prefer gate_compare.py for the iso-accuracy head-to-head since it is already leakage-free.

must_fix.issue: The reported conformal row does not faithfully represent CP-Router, and an 'equals MSP/Chow' claim is presented as unconditional. (a) sota_comparison.py:156-157 prints that the CP-Router set-size decision is 'monotone in top1prob => its frontier == MSP/Chow' and folds CP-Router INTO the MSP row — but this equivalence holds ONLY when the inclusion threshold 1-q_hat >= 0.5. At the tighter alphas CP-Router actually targets the rules diverge (verified on checkpoints: alpha=0.20 -> 2.0%, 0.15 -> 5.8%, 0.10 -> 9.7%, 0.05 -> 17.6% of the 8220 eval decisions differ). The stated '<=5-option MCQ' precondition is also false for our eval (opt_logprobs hold 5-10 options; 8 opts in 5307 rows), which breaks MSP-equivalence with sub-0.5 thresholds. (b) gate_alt_conformal_6datasets.py:82 (ec = sc > q_cp), gate_compare.py:85, and methods.py Conformal class all return 1-top1prob and build NO prediction set — they are pure MSP/Chow mislabeled 'conformal'. Only gate_alt_conformal.py builds a real set ({p>=1-q_hat}, escalate iff len!=1). (c) CP-Router's defining novelty — per-dataset FBE selection of alpha* to maximize set-size separability — is implemented (fbe(), set_size(), TAU_SET=1, a_star=argmax fbe) ONLY in the orphaned gate_ablation_bakeoff.py Part B (needs 32B-on-calibration labels) and feeds no reported row.
must_fix.fix: (1) Delete the sota_comparison.py:156-157 'monotone => == MSP/Chow' note; run gate_alt_conformal.py's genuine set-size rule as its own CP-Router row. (2) Implement CP-Router's actual alpha selection: port fbe() from gate_ablation_bakeoff.py:70-75 and choose alpha* = argmax_alpha FBE(set_sizes on the label-free eval/calib pool) per dataset, instead of fixing alpha at the 7B err-rate. (3) Relabel the MSP-collapsed arms (gate_alt_conformal_6datasets.py:82, gate_compare.py:85, methods.py Conformal) honestly as 'MSP/Chow', or make them build a real set. (4) If any 'equals MSP' caveat is kept, gate it: 'equal to MSP ONLY when 1-q_hat>=0.5; at FBE-selected alphas the set-size rule differs from MSP on up to ~18% of decisions, and the eval has 5-10 options.' Acceptable interim: report gate_alt_conformal.py (faithful score+set+quantile) and footnote that FBE adaptivity is not yet added.

should_fix: FrugalGPT-learned (LOW) — LABELING/FRAMING, not code. Our learned scorer reads ONLY per-letter logprob shape (margin/entropy/distribution in gate_alt_learned_gbm.py; 8 logprob-shape feats in gate_compare.py learned-correct), but FrugalGPT's g(q,a) is a DistilBERT reading query + GENERATED ANSWER TEXT. Sign/direction, threshold protocol (train-frozen tau in GBM; calib/test split in gate_compare) and leakage are all faithful. Fix: in the comparison text/table do not call it 'FrugalGPT' verbatim — call it 'FrugalGPT-style learned scorer (logprob-feature variant)' and add one sentence stating the input-modality delta (logprob distribution substitutes for query+answer text; a defensible, arguably stronger MCQA stand-in). Optionally add a true text-reliability variant on raw_output to show the logprob variant is not weaker. Optionally note we optimize at iso-accuracy/min-cost (dual of the paper's max-reward/budget-b).

ABC-agreement (LOW) — WORDING, not code. The binary disagree-escalate rule (acc_v2.py think_score, acc_compare.py M1b) is the exact k=2 special case of ABC's vote(x;H^k)<=theta, so the mechanism is faithful. But it is a CROSS-TIER (7B-nt vs 32B-nt) consistency check, not ABC's canonical intra-level same-cost ensemble vote, and on agreement we keep the 32B-nt answer (asymmetric, not an ensemble majority). The epsilon*(-m_32n) tiebreak blends ABC's vote rule with its score rule. Fix: in METHOD_ACC.md / METHOD_MATH.md describe it as a 'k=2 cross-tier instantiation of ABC's voting rule (plus its score rule)' with an asymmetric answer-on-agreement, so reviewers are not misled into thinking we reproduce ABC's intra-level ensemble-majority setup. No code change.

Confidence/DOCTOR/MSP/Chow (NONE, cosmetic) — implementations are faithful; only paper-text polish. (1) Note DOCTOR D_beta (1-max softmax) is decision-equivalent to MSP/Chow under threshold selection, so it is implicitly covered (a labeling-completeness gap, not a bug). (2) State softmax is renormalized over the answer options (MCQ label set) and stored top-20-letter mass is >=95% (median ~100%), so renorm vs full-vocab differs by <=0.025 gini. (3) Optionally rename sota_comparison.py 'margin(FrugalGPT)' to 'logprob-margin' to avoid conflating the logprob gap with prob_margin (both are already reported as separate rows, so no bias). None change any number.
acceptable: confidence-DOCTOR-MSP-Chow — faithful as-is. -top1prob == MSP and == Chow's 1-maxP up to sign (immaterial under thresholding); DOCTOR D_alpha verified monotone-equivalent to a Gini threshold (fires iff gini > gamma/(1+gamma)); our stored-softmax no-gradient setting is exactly DOCTOR's TBB scenario; entropy is standard Shannon entropy of the option distribution. Only cosmetic doc notes recommended.
ABC-agreement — mechanism faithful as-is (k=2 special case of ABC's vote<=theta rule); only METHOD_*.md wording needs to reflect cross-tier/asymmetric framing. No code change for faithfulness.

gate_compare.py's learned-defer and learned-correct arms — faithful as-is: Delta target = P(next-tier right) - P(this-tier right) matches Jitkrittum Diff-Prob/Diff-01; thresholds chosen on calib half and applied to disjoint test half; no leakage. (Distinct from the leaky metarouter_honest.py — that one is in must_fix.)

gate_alt_conformal.py (the set-size arm specifically) — faithful CORE as-is: LAC score 1-softmax(gold), finite-sample qhat via rank ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)), real set {p>=1-q_hat}, escalate iff |set|!=1. Its only gap is missing FBE alpha* selection (covered in must_fix as the CP-Router fix) — the score+set+quantile machinery itself needs no change.

FrugalGPT threshold protocols and leakage — acceptable as-is in both files (GBM train-frozen tau; gate_compare calib/test split). Only the 'FrugalGPT' label/input-modality framing needs a sentence (should_fix).
synthesis.summary: Most of our training-free baselines are mechanically faithful (confidence: MSP/Chow/entropy/DOCTOR-Gini are exact or verified monotone-equivalent to their papers; ABC's disagree-escalate is the correct k=2 special case of its voting rule; gate_compare.py's learned-defer/-correct match Jitkrittum's Diff-Prob target with a clean calib/test split; the gate_alt_conformal.py set-size arm has a faithful LAC score, finite-sample quantile, and real prediction set). But three issues bias or unsupport the published comparison and must be fixed before claims stand. First, there is NO faithful AutoMix anywhere — our self-verify is zero-shot single-pass and is only used as one feature inside a learned Delta-router, with no meta-verifier/POMDP and no threshold-on-v row, so 'margin beats AutoMix' is currently unsupported (HIGH). Second, metarouter_honest.py selects its operating point on the test half against test labels (the correct calib-side picker is defined but unused), inflating the absolute esc%@parity for every method in that file (MEDIUM). Third, the reported 'conformal' row is mostly an MSP/Chow collapse: three of four conformal arms build no prediction set, the 'set-size == MSP' claim only holds when 1-q_hat>=0.5 (rules diverge up to ~18% at the alphas CP-Router targets, and our eval has 5-10 options not <=5), and CP-Router's defining FBE alpha* novelty exists only in an orphaned bake-off (MEDIUM). The remaining deltas are framing-only and low-severity (call the learned scorer 'FrugalGPT-style logprob variant'; describe ABC as a cross-tier k=2 instantiation; minor DOCTOR/margin caption notes). Because gate_compare.py and sota_comparison.py feed the headline comparison and are directly touched by the conformal-relabeling, the new faithful AutoMix/CP-Router rows, and (if reported) the metarouter de-leak, the comparisons must be re-run after the fixes.
